Results.ReviewText: I just purchased my first BBQ in June of this year. It was a small, inexpensive gas grill from one of the local home supply stores. Very heavy duty and nice and thick which is good for grill masters in training so we don't loose our hamburgers!  I also like the tank meter to help me see how much gas I have left to grill with. The drip pan is HUGE compared to the inexpensive grill I bought so I can grill longer w/o having to empty it. I don't have the iGrill yet but I'm planning on getting one. It's great that Weber built in the option for this technology even on the smaller starter grills. Even though this grill was almost 3 times the price of the first grill I purchased I'm SO much happier! It was definitely worth the investment and I'm looking forward to using this grill for years to come!

Results.ReviewText:
I have owned several "top" rated grills. Living in the South, the grill is used year round, but my wife and I noted we were replacing our grill every two years. We remembered that Dad has had a Weber for years. So, in 2012 we bought a Weber Spirit grill.  We replaced the ignitor and the flavor shields. Here it is 2020 and we noted one of the burners was going. With eight years of wonderful food and easy maintenance, it was an easy decision, we needed another Weber.
The Weber Spirit II is the perfect size for us. A small footprint, it is easily maneuverable, as it goes from under cover on our Lanai to the open area for grilling. We enjoy the even heating, the easy operation and control, all add to our experience of a long life in the long grilling season that is the South.
